blurb: Japanese has several ways to tell someone they shouldn't do something — from a parent scolding a child to a formal workplace rule. This lesson covers the casual, spoken end: the kind you'd hear from a friend, a parent, or in everyday conversation. You'll recognize it when someone sets a boundary and know when to say "you shouldn't" versus "you must not."

formation.body:
Take the verb's て-form and drop て. Add ちゃ or じゃ, then いけない or ダメ.

たべる → たべて → たべちゃ + いけない
formation.title: Build from the て-form

formation.body:
If the て-form ends in で, use じゃ instead of ちゃ.

のむ → のんで → のんじゃ + いけない
formation.title: ちゃ vs じゃ

title: ちゃいけない・じゃいけない
pattern: ちゃいけない・じゃいけない
structure:
Take the verb's て-form and drop て. Add ちゃ or じゃ, then いけない or ダメ.

たべる → たべて → たべちゃ + いけない

If the て-form ends in で, use じゃ instead of ちゃ.

のむ → のんで → のんじゃ + いけない
